title: Domain Model

validation.research: Fowler's public Domain Model catalog establishes the executable data-plus-behavior pattern; Anemic Domain Model and Transaction Script distinguish alternative organizations of behavior. Data Mapper supports independence between model and storage representations. The Service Layer entry is correctly attributed to Randy Stafford. Evans's accessible DDD Reference Model-Driven Design discussion on printed page 6 connects implementation and domain language; Microsoft's official domain-model guide supports rich behavior, aggregate ownership, and invariants. Official Python documentation supports frozen records and the absence of enforced privacy from underscore names. The workshop scenario, policies, code, and diagrams are original teaching material. No inaccessible book chapter is claimed as consulted.

example_limits: A single-threaded in-memory workshop with fixed positive capacity, unique reservation references, derived remaining seats, and an explicit registration-closure policy. Public operations are the intended boundary; Python underscores do not enforce access control. Frozen booking records contain strings and integers. No persistence mapper, durable commit, concurrent capacity protection, authorization, automatic clock transition, external publication, or rollback of other effects is implemented. Domain Model is distinguished from the wider DDD approach, a database schema, and a mandatory State-pattern hierarchy.
publication: Local implementation only. No publishing, deployment, push, or pull request.
